But the summary has an internal contradiction in its framing, and some evidence is mis-cited or misleading, so an investigator would have to redo some of the work.","problems":["The headline calls the panel 'Healthy' while the card shows 35% of 99215 claims on patients with 2 or more conditions. It also says 'charts support the bill on their face' next to 'notes look inflated', which is muddled.","The summary says 25% below billed 'against 25% for the comparison providers', but the card gives an all-provider rate of 9.7% for 99215. This misstates the peer comparison and undercuts the 2/8 finding.","The summary says 'Only 3 of 30 random charts are below billed level', but one of the 3 examples (C0032211) is a 99214, so the 99215 below-billed count is 2 of 8 and the sentence mixes bases. The summary also treats a 2-of-8 sample as informative without flagging how small it is.","The headline says charts support the bill, yet the summary cites C0032261 and C0032349 as below billed. The next step puts those below-billed examples first among the charts to request, which is odd when those charts are already in hand. Requesting additional charts rather than re-reviewing the existing ones is only partly justified.","The numeric rationale is a dense list of rates with little interpretation. Examples of overlap are not shown, such as the 'late' and 'bulk created' notes that overlap with the cited claims. The 99215 claims on 0-condition patients are cited only in code-formatted examples (C0031664, C0031667 each have 1 condition, not 0), so the 'low complexity' examples are weak.","Missing items are not flagged, such as the lab or test lines absent for 6 notes, and which claims those are."]}
